correctness.rationale: For reduced positive-degree complex plane support, Bézout connects the components. The normalization map identifies finite fibers, lowering Euler characteristic by the sum of branch counts minus one; identifying finite subsets does not change H_2, so b_2 is the number of components. It follows that b_* = 2 + 2 sum g_i + sum_p(b_p−1). Substitution of the genus–delta and Milnor–branch identities and splitting b_p−1 into the within-component contributions and k_p−1 gives exactly the stated local defect after Bézout. At k_p≥2, the intersection sum is at least binom(k_p,2); vanishing defect forces k_p=2 and multiplicity one there, and zero component Milnor numbers force smoothness. Successively choosing general components gives these transverse double points and avoids prior crossings. The fixed-r objective depends positively on sum d_i², strictly improved by transferring a unit from a smaller degree >1 to a larger one. Strict convexity in r leaves the endpoint comparison: the reducible endpoint difference is (d−5)(d−2)/2; the global maximum is 2,3,5,8 for degrees 1–4 and d²−3d+4 thereafter. The quartic global tie and the quintic reducible-only tie are correct. A nonreduced divisor has support of degree ≤d−1 and inherits its Betti numbers; M(d) is increasing and M(d−1)=d²−5d+8 is below the reducible threshold by d−1 for d≥6, justifying the certificate for all divisors. Independently checked 271 positive-degree partitions through degree 12 by recursive generation and the global Milnor formula at the nodal extremizer (python /workspace/branches/independent_math_checks.py, section 3). This is an algebraic finite check, not a topological proof. Inspected the frozen checks/betti_envelope.py without executing it.

value.rationale: Finite evaluation of the natural plane linear-system supremum is not supplied by its limiting volume. The partition envelope identifies exactly how distributing component degrees can beat a smooth curve in low degree, and the reducible envelope gives a practical sharp sufficient Betti threshold for reduced irreducibility. The quartic and quintic ties arise from competing geometries, not from an arbitrary set of tabulated degrees.
